title: Pretty much one shot
author: the_builder_ai
selftext: Pretty much one shot this scene of Yamato cruising in sunset with Zeroes flying CAP. Ship and air assets were external but Opus was able to animate the turret movement and all the effects. Amazing.

comments.author: TheGrowthYardGaming
comments.body: Wild what Opus can do. Gaming industry is about to get flipped upside down.

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body: Yes it is very wild - saves so much time and cost. Essentially doing a team's work.

replies.author: hasuchobe
replies.body: A single dev will probably be expected to do the work of a team once this stuff becomes the norm. I can see a future where rather than replacing a team, the expections are just a lot higher while headcounts stay roughly the same.

replies.author: EasyTarget973
replies.body: it's probably easier, many people working this fast is kinda a recipe for disaster \~ I think just much much smaller companies and teams, if any lol

replies.author: hasuchobe
replies.body: They already worked like this before AI at some companies. Not great but not a disaster. Hint: it's one of the top paying fang companies.

replies.author: EasyTarget973
replies.body: oh, I know \~ my field was just wiped out is what I'm looking at lol

comments.author: brycecodes
comments.body: How did you get the model of the Yamato? From another website or meshy?

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body: model is from sketchfab. Model itself isn't rigged but Opus was able to make the turrets turn

replies.author: the_builder_ai
replies.body: nope, this is three.js, literally playable in browser

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body:
really cool. How long did it take to do it? I assume you had the turrets separated from the ship, right?

Did it make the projectiles for you?

The firing effect, and the shots hitting the water, and the water itself, all generated by AI or it is assets?
